notes: v1.14.541 — LEGACY-RETIRE STAGE 3.2b: FIVE SHEETS RECLAIM 106px. --action-stripe-reserve is deleted along with the ' + var(--action-stripe-reserve)' term in all five rules that read it: .sop-sheet-inner, .rm-device-inner, .rm-sheet-inner, .va-sheet-inner and .ge-inner. They now pay calc(safe-bottom + 20px) — or 16px for .ge-inner — which is the exact shape the rest of the file already uses at :3583 and :3749, so this lands the five odd rules back on the house convention rather than inventing a new one. ⭐ This is the REDESIGN-visible half of the action-stripe removal, split from .540 deliberately: .540 deleted a bar visible only under ?legacy=1, this frees layout in both houses, and one visible change per ship means they cannot ride together. The reserve had been dead in the redesign for as long as body.rd hid the stripe — 106px of bottom padding on five full-screen sheets, reserving room for something that could not render. ⛔ SAFETY CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED, because removing bottom padding is exactly the .532 shape: all five consumers sit inside inset:0 overlays at z-index 150–200 while #rd-botnav is z-index 40, so the nav is UNDERNEATH them and none of this was ever nav clearance. None of the five sheets contains a sticky or fixed footer. And no other persistently-fixed element sits above them at the bottom — every high-z fixed surface in the file is its own full-screen overlay or an action bar belonging to one. The stripe at z-index 800 was the only thing this reserve ever cleared, and .540 deleted it. The cross-reference at :9287 that cited this token as the worked example of 'name every term' is corrected: the example is gone, the rule is not.
